steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large glass baking dish, marinate chicken in butter, parsley, scallions, mushrooms, chives, garlic, salt, and pepper for 1 hour at room temperature or several hours in the fridge.
If refrigerated, bring chicken to room temperature before baking.
Heavily coat each piece of chicken with breadcrumbs.
Bake for about ½ hour (approximately 30 minutes) until chicken is cooked through and breadcrumbs are golden brown. Don't crowd chicken.
tips: Pro Tip: Letting the chicken marinate allows the flavors to penetrate the meat, resulting in a more flavorful dish.
Variation: You can substitute chicken thighs for a juicier result.
Pro Tip: Make sure the butter is cooled before adding to prevent cooking the chicken prematurely.
baked-chicken-with-herbs-and-mushrooms.title: Baked Chicken With Herbs and Mushrooms

ingredients.item: chopped fresh oregano, or 1 tablespoon dried

steps: In a Dutch oven, over medium heat, heat the oil. Add the onion and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the celery, carrot, and garlic and cook for 5 minutes more.
Add the pancetta and cook for 5 minutes, then add the beef and cook until brown.
Add the wine and the remaining ingredients (tomatoes, tomato paste, milk, red pepper, oregano, parsley, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg) and simmer for 45 minutes.
Serve with cooked fettuccine. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
bolognese.title: Fettuccine With Bolognese Sauce

ingredients.item: green cabbage, cored and sliced into ribbons

steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.

Place the bratwurst on the prepared baking sheet. Roast for 20 to 22 minutes, flipping once halfway through, until deeply browned on the outside and cooked through. An instant-read thermometer should read 160°F at the center.

While the brats roast, place the potatoes (whole, unpeeled) in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until fork-tender, about 20 to 22 minutes. Drain and let cool just enough to handle, then peel and slice into ½-inch rounds. Keep warm.

Melt the butter with a drizzle of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and caraway seeds and cook until fragrant. Add the cabbage and toss to coat. Pour in some chicken stock and a little vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and cover. Cook over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is tender and silky. Uncover for the last 5 minutes to cook off excess liquid.

In a skillet over medium heat, cook the bacon until crispy and the fat has rendered, about 6 to 7 minutes. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside. To the bacon fat in the pan, add the remaining olive oil, remaining apple cider vinegar, mustard, sugar, and remaining chicken stock. Whisk together and warm over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes until combined into a glossy dressing.

Pour the warm dressing over the sliced potatoes and toss gently to coat — the potatoes should absorb the dressing while still warm. Fold in the reserved bacon and the chives or parsley. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve each roasted brat alongside a generous scoop of warm potato salad and a pile of braised cabbage. Offer spicy brown mustard on the side.
bratwurst.title: Bratwurst With German Potato Salad and Braised Cabbage

ingredients.item: boneless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into 1½-inch pieces

steps: In a large bowl, combine half the Greek yogurt (reserve the rest for the sauce) with half the garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and coriander, plus the cayenne, half the ginger, half the garlic, and the salt. Add the chicken and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 60 minutes, or overnight for best results.

Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine with 2¼ cups water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam, covered, for 5 more minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the neutral oil in a large heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Remove the chicken from the marinade (don't wipe it clean) and sear in batches for 2 to 6 minutes per side until browned. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining oil to the pan over medium heat. Add the remaining garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and coriander and toast, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Add the onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until softened and golden. Add the remaining ginger and garlic and cook 1 minute more.

Add the bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until slightly softened. Return the seared chicken and any resting juices to the pan and stir to coat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through. The onions and peppers will release enough moisture to keep things from sticking — add a small splash of water if needed.

Reduce heat to low. Temper the remaining yogurt by stirring a spoonful of the hot curry into it, then stir the mixture back into the pan. Add the almond butter and stir until fully incorporated and the sauce is smooth and creamy. Do not boil after adding the yogurt.

Stir in the peas and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just heated through. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt. Serve over the basmati rice, garnished with cilantro and lemon or lime wedges for squeezing over.
chicken-curry.title: Chicken Curry

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breasts, pounded thin

steps: Pound the chicken breasts to about ¼-inch thickness between plastic wrap. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Place the flour in a shallow dish. In a separate shallow bowl, beat the eggs with a splash of water until smooth.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve ½ cup pasta water, then drain and set aside.

Heat the olive oil and 2 tablespoons of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shake off the excess, then dip in the egg mixture. Cook in batches for 3 to 8 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and tent loosely with foil.

In the same skillet over medium heat, add the wine and let it reduce by half, about 5 minutes. Add the chicken stock and lemon juice, then stir in the capers and lemon rounds. Simmer for 3 minutes, then swirl in the remaining butter to finish the sauce.

While the sauce simmers, heat a separate pan with a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant. Add the broccoli florets and sauté for 5 to 6 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Season with salt.

Return the chicken to the skillet and spoon sauce over top, warming for 1 to 2 minutes. Divide the linguine among plates. Place chicken over pasta and spoon plenty of sauce and capers over everything. Garnish with parsley and serve the broccoli alongside.
francese.title: Chicken Francese

grilled-chicken-and-ziti-summer-salad.description: A refreshing pasta salad featuring grilled chicken, colorful vegetables, and a tangy lemon-Dijon dressing. Perfect for summer gatherings, potlucks, or meal prep. This crowd-pleasing dish can be served warm or cold.

ingredients.item: large red bell peppers (cut into ½" dice)
Kalamata olives, pitted, drained, sliced thin

steps: Grill chicken 8 minutes per side or until springy to touch. Transfer to a baking dish and sprinkle with lemon juice. Let cool.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Refresh under cold water and let cool (turn frequently to prevent sticking).
In a large bowl, toss together the ziti, bell pepper, celery, onion, olives, and dill.
Remove cooled chicken from dish (saving juice) and slice thin. Add sliced chicken to salad.
To the lemon juice in the baking dish, add vinegar, mayo, mustard, salt, and pepper. Whisk well.
Add olive oil in a stream, whisking the whole time, to create an emulsified dressing. Add dressing to pasta salad and toss well to combine.
tips: Pro Tip: Turn the pasta frequently while cooling to prevent it from clumping together.
Variation: Add capers for an extra briny, Mediterranean flavor.
Pro Tip: The dressing can be made ahead and refrigerated. Whisk before using if it separates.
Serving Suggestion: This salad can be served immediately while slightly warm or chilled for a few hours for a cold salad.
grilled-chicken-and-ziti-summer-salad.title: Grilled Chicken and Ziti Summer Salad

kielbasa-white-bean-and-barley-stew.description: A hearty, smoky stew with kielbasa, white beans, kale, and barley for body.

ingredients.item: large kale leaves, stemmed and chopped

notes: To make with pearled farro: Swap the ¾ cup pearl barley for ¾ cup pearled farro, rinsed. Farro cooks faster, so in step 3 simmer for 25 to 30 minutes instead of 40, until chewy and tender. Keep the 6 cups of broth and add a splash more at the end if the stew gets too thick.
Whole-grain (not pearled) farro takes 40 to 50 minutes, about the same as barley, or soak it overnight to shorten the cook time.
Farro also keeps absorbing broth as it sits, so thin leftovers with broth or water when reheating. For a brothier stew, cook the farro separately and spoon it into each bowl.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the kielbasa and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook until softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more, until fragrant.
Stir in the barley and toast for 1 minute, then add the broth, bay leaf, and thyme. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook until the barley is tender, about 40 minutes.
Stir the kielbasa back in along with the beans. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld and the stew thicken slightly.
Stir in the kale and cook until just wilted, about 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, then stir in the vinegar and season with the salt and pepper to taste.
tips: Barley thickens the stew as it sits, so leftovers will be even heartier. Thin with a splash of broth when reheating.
A parmesan rind simmered in with the broth adds extra depth.
kielbasa-white-bean-and-barley-stew.title: Kielbasa, White Bean and Barley Stew

lemon-breadcrumb-haddock-with-roasted-po.description: A one-pan supper: crisp roasted potatoes and sunchokes with baked haddock under a buttery lemon breadcrumb crust.

ingredients.item: potatoes, scrubbed and cut into ¾-inch chunks
sunchokes, scrubbed and cut into ¾-inch chunks
kosher salt, divided, plus black pepper
lemons (1 zested and juiced, 1 cut into wedges)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rimmed sheet pan inside. Toss the potatoes and sunchokes with the olive oil, half the salt, and pepper. Spread on the hot pan in a single layer and roast for 15 minutes, stirring once, until they begin to brown.
While the vegetables roast, stir together the breadcrumbs, melted butter, zest of one lemon, garlic, and a pinch of salt.
Pat the haddock dry and season both sides with the remaining salt. Squeeze a little juice from the zested lemon over the fish.

Push the vegetables to the sides of the pan and set the fish in the center. Press the crumb mixture onto the top of each piece. Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the fish flakes easily (about 130°F inside).
Sprinkle with parsley and serve right away with the lemon wedges.
tips: Brush the fish lightly with Dijon mustard before adding the crumbs to help them stick and add flavor.
If the vegetables aren't quite tender when the fish is done, leave them in a few more minutes while the fish rests.
For a thicker piece of fish, add 2 to 3 minutes. If your breadcrumbs are already seasoned, cut back on the salt.
Sunchokes brown quickly once cut, so hold them in lemon water if prepping ahead.
lemon-breadcrumb-haddock-with-roasted-po.title: Lemon Breadcrumb Haddock With Roasted Potatoes and Sunchokes

one-pot-spanish-rice-with-chicken-thighs.description: A quick weeknight one-pot using jarred sofrito as the flavor base.
notes: If your sofrito is on the sweeter side, a squeeze of lime at the end helps balance it.
Bone-in thighs work too; add about 10 extra minutes of covered simmer time.
steps: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet or shallow pot over medium-high heat. Sear the thighs 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden but not cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the sofrito to the same pan and cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir to coat every grain in the sofrito, toasting for 1 to 2 minutes.

Pour in the broth, then stir in the smoked paprika and cumin. Bring to a boil, nestle the chicken (and any juices) back into the rice, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Simmer about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
If using, stir in the olives and peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking, then re-cover.
Turn off the heat and let sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over the top.
one-pot-spanish-rice-with-chicken-thighs.title: One-Pot Spanish Rice With Chicken Thighs

ingredients.item: hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
broccoli rabe, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. It should taste like mild seawater — this is your only chance to season the pasta itself.
Add the broccoli rabe to the boiling water and blanch for 2 minutes until bright green and just tender. Remove with a slotted spoon or tongs and set aside — keep the water boiling for the pasta.

Add the orecchiette to the same boiling water and cook according to package directions until 10 minutes shy of al dente — it will finish cooking in the pan. Before draining, scoop out at least 1 cup reserved pasta water. Drain and set aside.

While the pasta cooks, heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large, wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it into chunks, for 6 to 7 minutes until well browned and cooked through. Don't over-stir — let it develop color. Transfer sausage to a plate, leaving the fat in the pan.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining olive oil to the pan. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until the garlic is golden and fragrant but not burnt. Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, about 2 minutes. Add the chicken stock and stir to combine.

Add the drained orecchiette, the browned sausage, and the blanched broccoli rabe to the skillet. Toss everything together over medium heat, adding reserved pasta water a splash at a time to loosen the sauce and help it coat the pasta. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the pasta is al dente and the sauce is silky.

Remove from heat. Add the butter and half of the Pecorino Romano and toss vigorously until the butter melts and the sauce comes together. Season with salt and pepper. Divide among bowls and top with the remaining Pecorino Romano.
orecchiette-with-sausage.title: Orecchiette With Sausage

pot-roast.description: A well-marbled chuck-eye roast creates the perfect pot roast. Splitting the roast along its natural seams allows for trimming excess fat, and working with two smaller roasts means the finished dish is ready faster. This classic comfort food delivers tender, flavorful beef with rich gravy.

ingredients.item: (3½- to 4-pound) boneless beef chuck-eye roast, pulled into 2 pieces at natural seam and trimmed of large knobs of fat
fresh thyme, plus ¼ teaspoon chopped

steps: Season pieces of meat with 1 tablespoon salt, place on wire rack set in rimmed baking sheet, and let stand at room temperature for 1 hour.

Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 300 degrees. Melt butter in Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and beginning to brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Add carrot and celery; continue to cook, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in 1 cup broth, ½ cup wine, tomato paste, bay leaf, and thyme sprig.
Pat beef dry with paper towels and season with pepper. Tie 3 pieces of kitchen twine around each piece of meat to form even shape.

Nestle meat on top of vegetables. Cover pot tightly with large piece of aluminum foil and cover with lid. Transfer to oven. Cook beef until fully tender and fork slips easily in and out of meat, 3½ to 4 hours, turning meat halfway through cooking.

Transfer roasts to carving board and tent loosely with foil. Strain liquid through fine-mesh strainer into 4-cup liquid measuring cup. Discard bay leaf and thyme sprig. Transfer vegetables to blender. Let liquid settle for 5 minutes, then skim fat; add 1 to 2 cups beef broth to bring liquid amount to 3 cups. Add liquid to blender and blend until smooth, about 2 minutes. Transfer sauce to medium saucepan and bring to simmer over medium heat.

Meanwhile, remove twine from roasts and slice against grain into ½-inch-thick slices. Transfer meat to serving platter. Stir remaining ¼ cup wine, chopped thyme, and vinegar into gravy and season with salt and pepper to taste. Spoon half of gravy over meat; pass remaining gravy separately.
tips: Pro Tip: Chilling the whole cooked pot roast overnight improves its flavor and makes it moister and easier to slice.

Variation: For Classic Pot Roast with Root Vegetables — add 1 pound carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces, 1 pound parsnips, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces, and 1½ pounds red potatoes, peeled and halved lengthwise, each half quartered, to pot after cooking beef for 3 hours. Continue to cook until beef is fully tender, 30 minutes to 1 hour longer. Transfer large pieces of carrot, parsnip, and potato to serving platter using slotted spoon, cover tightly with aluminum foil, and proceed with recipe as directed.
pot-roast.title: Pot Roast

saffron-chicken-with-rice-and-dates.description: North African staples transform this simple supper. A flavorful combination of saffron-spiced chicken with sweet dates and aromatic rice.

ingredients.item: skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Sprinkle chicken with ¼ teaspoon salt and pepper. Add chicken to pan, and sauté 5 minutes, browning on all sides. Remove chicken from pan; keep warm.

Add onion, ⅛ teaspoon saffron, and garlic to pan; sauté 5 minutes or until onion is tender. Stir in reserved chicken, tomato juice, and dates; cover. Reduce heat to low, and cook 15 minutes. Uncover; cook 10 minutes. Remove from heat; keep warm.

Combine ¼ teaspoon salt, ⅛ teaspoon saffron, 2 cups water, and rice in a saucepan, bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 20 minutes or until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork. Serve the chicken mixture over rice mixture. Garnish with sliced green onions and lemon wedges, if desired.
tips: Pro Tip: Crushing the saffron threads helps release their flavor and color more effectively.
Variation: You can substitute chicken thighs for a richer flavor.
saffron-chicken-with-rice-and-dates.title: Saffron Chicken With Rice and Dates

ingredients.item: Pack of sausage (andouille, Italian, or chorizo)
Vinaigrette (olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, pepper)

steps: Cook rice. Heat beans on the stovetop, adding cumin and bay leaf.
Make a generous vinaigrette in a serving bowl. Chop tomatoes, celery, and red onion and add. Let sit for at least 20 minutes.
Cook sausage in the oven; preheat to 425°F, cook 20 minutes.
Remove sausage and chop. Add along with remaining ingredients.
sausage-with-latin-salad.title: Sausage With Latin Salad

ingredients.item: hot Italian sausage links, cut into 1-inch pieces
cherry peppers (hot or sweet), halved and seeded
Crusty bread or roasted potatoes, for serving

steps: Pat the chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels — this is key for a good sear. Season aggressively on all sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken skin-side down without moving for 6 to 10 minutes until deeply golden. Flip and sear the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, add the sausage and cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Transfer to the plate with the chicken.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat from the pan. Add the onion and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cherry peppers and cook another 2 minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the wine and scrape up all the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Add the chicken stock, cherry pepper brine, white wine vinegar, and rosemary sprigs. Return the chicken and sausage to the pan. The liquid should come about halfway up the chicken — add a splash more stock if needed.

Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and braise for 30 minutes, then uncover and cook another 10 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has reduced to a glossy, tangy pan gravy.

Remove the rosemary sprigs. Swirl in the butter to enrich the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning — add a splash more vinegar or brine if you want more tang. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread or roasted potatoes to soak up all that sauce.
scarpariello.title: Chicken Scarpariello

ingredients.item: bell peppers (mixed colors), sliced into strips
hearts of palm, drained and sliced into rounds

steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, oregano, and salt and pepper. Place the steak in a shallow dish or zip-lock bag and coat with the marinade. Let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 4 hours.

Combine the hearts of palm, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and most of the cilantro in a bowl. Drizzle with the lime juice and olive oil for the salad, season with salt and pepper, and toss to combine. Set aside to lightly marinate while you cook everything else.

Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the onion and cook for about 11 minutes until starting to soften and char at the edges. Add the bell peppers and cook for another 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender with good color. Season with salt and pepper and keep warm.

Position an oven rack about 4 inches from the broiler and preheat the broiler on high. Remove the steak from the marinade and pat lightly dry. Place on a foil-lined rimmed baking sheet. Broil skirt steak for 3 to 8 minutes per side, or flank steak for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until charred at the edges and medium-rare to medium inside.
Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let rest for 5 to 6 minutes. Slice thinly against the grain at a slight diagonal — this is critical for tenderness.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and place in a 300°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes, or char individually over a gas burner for 30 seconds per side. Keep wrapped until serving.

Lay out the steak, peppers and onions, cheddar, sour cream, and avocado for building. Top the salad with the remaining cilantro. Let everyone assemble their own fajitas and serve the hearts of palm salad alongside.
tips: Skirt is fattier than flank, works better if available.
Broil about 4 inches from the heat.
Consider cotija and jalapeños.
steak-fajitas.title: Steak Fajitas

sheet-pan-chicken-and-potatoes-with-feta.title: Sheet-Pan Chicken and Potatoes With Feta, Lemon and Dill

ingredients.item: lemon juice (from about half a lemon)
small bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (4 to 6 thighs)
small Yukon gold potatoes (about 1 pound), cut into ¾-inch pieces

steps: In a medium bowl, whisk 2 tablespoons oil with 1 tablespoon lemon juice, the garlic, oregano, 1 teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper. Add the chicken thighs toss to coat. Let the chicken marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 8 hours, covered, in the refrigerator.

Heat the oven to 425 degrees. On a sheet pan, drizzle the diced potatoes with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and sprinkle with ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper; toss well and move to one side of the pan. Pat the chicken thighs dry and place them, evenly spaced, on the other side of the pan.

Roast for 15 minutes, toss the potatoes, then return everything to the oven and roast until the chicken is cooked through, the skin is golden brown, and the potatoes are tender, 15 to 25 more minutes, depending on the size of the thighs. If the potatoes are not quite tender, remove the chicken thighs to a plate to rest, and return the potatoes to the oven to roast until tender, another 5 to 10 minutes.

Place the chicken and potatoes on a serving platter, and sprinkle them 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Scatter the feta and dill over the potatoes, sprinkle the whole dish with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

pasta-alla-vodka.title: Pasta Alla Vodka

ingredients.item: grated Grana Padano or Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil (2 heaping tablespoons kosher salt to about 7 quarts water). Add the pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.

Meanwhile, prepare the sauce: Heat the oil in a deep 12-inch skillet or pot over medium. Add the pancetta, if using, and fry until crispy, stirring occasionally, 3 to 5 minutes. Add the onion, garlic and red-pepper flakes and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent, about 3 minutes. Turn the heat to medium-low, add the vodka and cook until reduced by half, 2 to 3 minutes.

Stir in the tomatoes and then fill the can halfway with water and swish it around to loosen up any leftover tomatoes; add a quarter to half of the water to the pan. Simmer until the sauce begins to thicken, about 10 minutes, and season with salt and pepper. If you prefer your sauce a little looser, go ahead and add the remaining water and simmer 2 to 3 minutes more. Reduce heat to low, add the cream and cook, stirring, until the sauce becomes an even pinkish-rust color, about 1 minute.
Stir in the cooked pasta and ¼ cup cheese; toss to coat. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Divide among bowls, top with additional cheese, if desired, and sprinkle with the oregano and parsley.

french-potato-salad.title: French Potato Salad
french-potato-salad.description: A straightforward, old-fashioned French potato salad with chives and tarragon.

ingredients.item: yellow-fleshed potatoes, such as Yukon Gold
fruity extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed

steps: Put potatoes in a large pot, cover with water, salt generously and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to a brisk simmer. Cook for about 30 minutes, until cooked through but firm. (Test with a skewer or paring knife.) Drain.

Holding each potato in a paper towel or tea towel to keep from burning your fingers, peel the thin skins while still warm with a paring knife (they come away easily). Cut peeled potatoes into thick slices (about ⅜ inch) and place in a large low bowl.

In a small bowl, add vinegar and mustard, stirring to dissolve. Whisk in olive oil and season to taste with salt and pepper. Pour over warm sliced potatoes and very gently and briefly toss with hands, taking care not to break the slices. Sprinkle with a little salt and leave to cool at room temperature.

When potatoes have cooled, add tarragon leaves and chives (save some of the herbs for garnish) and very gently toss again. Taste, adjust for salt and toss one more time. The salad should be fairly oily; drizzle with a little more oil if necessary. Serve at room temperature, sprinkled with reserved herbs.

baked-risotto-with-greens-and-peas.title: Baked Risotto With Greens and Peas
baked-risotto-with-greens-and-peas.description: A baked risotto that skips the constant stirring of traditional recipes, laden with kale, spinach and peas.

ingredients.item: green or lacinato kale (about ⅓ bunch), stems separated and thinly sliced, leaves stacked and cut into ¼-inch-thick ribbons (about 4 packed cups)
low-sodium chicken, vegetable or mushroom broth
grated Parmesan (3 ounces), plus more for garnish

steps: Heat oven to 375 degrees. In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, 1 minute. Add rice, season with salt and pepper, and stir until coated in oil and lightly toasted, 2 minutes.
Add kale, season with salt and pepper, and stir until wilted, 30 seconds. Add broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Cover and bake until almost all of the liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, about 20 minutes.

Stir in spinach and peas until spinach is wilted. Add Parmesan, butter and lemon juice, and stir until well blended and saucy. (Liquid will continue to absorb as risotto sits.) Season with salt and pepper. Serve in bowls, topped with more Parmesan.
notes: Use vegetable or mushroom broth to keep it vegetarian.

pasta-amatriciana.title: Pasta Amatriciana
pasta-amatriciana.description: A traditional Roman pasta with a sauce of guanciale (cured pork jowl), tomato and Pecorino Romano.

ingredients.item: guanciale or pancetta, chopped into ¼-inch cubes (¾ cup)
(28-ounce) whole tomatoes, crushed with your hands in a bowl
black pepper, plus more to taste
grated Pecorino Romano, plus more for garnish

steps: In a large (12-inch) skillet, heat olive oil over medium. Add guanciale and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden, about 5 minutes. To the skillet, add tomatoes, black pepper and red-pepper flakes, and season with salt. Cook, stirring occasionally and smashing tomatoes with the back of a wooden spoon, until tomatoes have broken down and sauce is thickened, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted water, cook pasta according to package directions until just shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup of the pasta cooking water and drain.

Add pasta, tomato sauce and ½ cup of pasta cooking water back to the large pasta pot and stir vigorously over medium-high heat until pasta is evenly coated in the sauce, about 1 minute. (Add more pasta water if sauce is dry.) Remove from heat, stir in the cheese and season to taste with salt.
Divide pasta among bowls and garnish with more Pecorino Romano and black pepper.
tips: Substitution: use 2 pints (about 1½ pounds) cherry tomatoes, halved, in place of the canned tomatoes. Add them after the guanciale is golden, raise the heat to medium-high, and cook until they burst and slump, smashing them with the spoon, about 10 to 12 minutes. Fresh tomatoes give a brighter, chunkier sauce with less liquid, so lean on the pasta water when tossing.

sesame-chicken-with-cashews-and-dates.title: Sesame Chicken With Cashews and Dates

ingredients.item: 2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into about 12 “coins”
scallions (white and green parts), cut into 2-inch lengths
dried red chiles, or ½ teaspoon chile flakes
boneless chicken thighs (preferably skin on, but skinless is O.K.), cut into 2-inch chunks
fresh basil or cilantro leaves, or a combination
Rice vinegar or lime juice, to taste

steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper while you heat a 12-inch skillet or wok over high heat until it’s very hot, at least 2 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons of the sesame oil and swirl the pan; the oil should thin on contact. When the oil is hot, add the ginger, garlic, scallions and chile. Stir-fry until the garlic is golden at the edges, 2 to 3 minutes.

Add the 2 remaining tablespoon oil, chicken and cashews, and stir fry until it starts to brown, 4 to 5 minutes (turn down the heat if the cashews are browning too quickly). Add the rice wine, soy sauce and dates; simmer until the sauce reduces to a syrupy consistency and the chicken cooks through, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in the herbs, sprinkle with rice vinegar or lime juice, and serve over rice.

tacos-de-carnitas.title: Tacos de Carnitas

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, either butt or picnic
large onion, chopped, plus finely chopped onion for garnish
crushed dried oregano leaves, preferably Mexican
small corn tortillas, warmed, for serving

steps: Trim any thick fat from surface of pork. Cut meat into 1-inch cubes, discarding any that are pure fat. Put pork in a large pot. Add enough water to cover by 2 inches, orange zest, garlic, chopped onion, red pepper flakes, cinnamon, bay leaves, oregano, 1½ teaspoons salt and the cloves.

Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Skim off any scum that forms on surface. Simmer uncovered for 1½ hours, until pork is very soft; add water if necessary to keep meat submerged. Season with salt, then continue to cook until water has evaporated, about 30 minutes. Cook a little longer to fry meat slightly; cook even longer if you prefer crisper meat. Stir often and add a bit of water if meat sticks or seems about to burn.
Remove bay leaves and cinnamon stick. Spoon a few tablespoons of carnitas onto each tortilla. Top each taco with cilantro, finely chopped onion and salsa. Serve.

the-silver-palates-chicken-marbella.title: The Silver Palate’s Chicken Marbella
the-silver-palates-chicken-marbella.description: The classic from “The Silver Palate Cookbook” by Sheila Lukins and Julee Rosso.

ingredients.item: capers, with a bit of juice
fresh oregano, chopped, or ¼ cup dried oregano

steps: In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, vinegar, prunes, olives, capers and juice, bay leaves, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Add the chicken pieces and turn to coat. Refrigerate overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Arrange the chicken in a single layer in a shallow roasting pan; spoon the marinade over it evenly. Pour in the wine and sprinkle the chicken with the brown sugar.

Bake until the thigh pieces yield clear yellow juice when pricked with a fork, 50 to 60 minutes, basting two or three times with the pan juices once the chicken begins to brown. (When basting, do not brush off the sugar. If the chicken browns too quickly, cover lightly with foil.)

Transfer the chicken pieces to a warm serving platter and top with the prunes, olives and capers; keep warm. Place the roasting pan over medium heat and bring the pan juices to a boil. Reduce to about ½ cup. Strain into a heatproof bowl, add the parsley and pour over the chicken.
notes: Marinate the chicken overnight before baking.

source.label: NYT Cooking, from The Silver Palate Cookbook

roasted-sweet-potatoes-with-smoked-papri.title: Roasted Sweet Potatoes With Smoked Paprika

ingredients.item: large sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes
large Spanish onion, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Heat oven to 425 degrees. Combine the sweet potatoes, onion and garlic in a large bowl, and drizzle the olive oil over it, then toss to coat. Sprinkle the salt, pepper and smoked paprika over the potatoes, and toss again to coat. Tip the potatoes onto a sheet pan or into a shallow casserole, then cover it with foil.

Roast the potatoes in the oven, tossing occasionally, until they are soft at the center and beginning to crisp at the edges, approximately 30 to 40 minutes. Serve hot, drizzled with burned-scallion crema if you like.
notes: Burned-scallion crema is a separate NYT Cooking recipe.

umbrian-style-chicken-alla-cacciatora.title: Umbrian-Style Chicken Alla Cacciatora

ingredients.item: small chicken (about 2½ pounds), cut into serving pieces, or use bone-in, skin-on thighs and drumsticks
good-quality brine-cured olives, black or green, with pits

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large non-stick pan. Add chicken pieces and sear over medium heat until golden on all sides, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a plate and wipe the pan clean before proceeding.

Turn heat to low, add remaining 1 teaspoon oil, and return the chicken to the pan. Add onions and stir frequently until caramelized, about 18 minutes. Add minced garlic, capers, olives, rosemary sprig and sage leaves. Season with just a sprinkle of salt and black pepper.

After a couple of minutes, when everything smells fragrant, add wine. Cover and simmer very slowly until the chicken is tender and cooked through (165 degrees). Start checking the temperature of the chicken after 15 minutes to avoid overcooking. Add some water if the sauce gets too dry while simmering.
When ready to serve, reheat if necessary, then add lemon juice and zest and balsamic vinegar. Taste and add more lemon if desired. Remove the rosemary sprig and serve.

chicken-vesuvio.title: Chicken Vesuvio

ingredients.item: large russet potatoes (about 2¼ pounds), scrubbed, halved lengthwise, then cut into long 1-inch-wide wedges

steps: Heat oven to 425 degrees. In a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, toss the potato wedges with 3 tablespoons olive oil and ½ teaspoon oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Spread the potatoes out in an even layer. (It’s OK if some overlap). Bake, tossing gently once halfway through cooking, until the edges begin to brown, and the potatoes can be pierced with a fork but are still quite firm, about 30 minutes. (They’ll finish cooking with the chicken.)

While potatoes roast, prepare the chicken: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and the remaining 1 teaspoon oregano. In a large 12-inch skillet, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high until it shimmers. Working in batches if necessary, cook the chicken, skin-side down, until it is golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate.

Reduce heat to medium-low, add the butter and garlic to the skillet and cook until the butter is melted and the garlic is fragrant and just beginning to brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Add the chicken stock and wine to the skillet, bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes. Add the peas. Pour the mixture evenly over the potatoes, then gently stir to combine. Place chicken on top of the cooked potato mixture, skin-side up. Drizzle any reserved chicken juices on top.

Bake until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender, 20 to 25 minutes. Turn on the oven’s broiler function, and broil until the chicken skin is golden brown and crisp, 1 to 2 minutes. Drizzle with lemon juice, and sprinkle with parsley. Serve immediately, with plenty of the pan juices spooned over the chicken and potatoes, and crusty bread on the side.

craig-claibornes-beef-stroganoff.title: Craig Claiborne’s Beef Stroganoff

ingredients.item: beef tenderloin or boneless sirloin of beef, trimmed of all exterior fat and cut into 2-by-¼-by-¼-inch strips
beef or chicken stock, ideally homemade

steps: Combine the flour, salt and pepper. Dredge the meat in the mixture.
Brown the meat in one-quarter cup of the butter in a saucepan. Remove meat from the pan and set aside.
Add the onion to the pan and sauté until transparent. Add the mushrooms and remaining butter and sauté 3 to 5 minutes longer.
Add the beef stock or bouillon and bring to a boil. The preparation, to this point, may be done ahead.
Add the meat to the sauce and cook until meat is tender but not overcooked, 3 to 10 minutes, stirring often.

Combine sour cream, tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce. Add some of the beef sauce to sour cream mixture. Return to pan and heat meat and sauce, stirring. Do not boil. Sprinkle with parsley. Serve with buttered parsley noodles.

pasta-salad-with-roasted-eggplant-chile-.title: Pasta Salad With Roasted Eggplant, Chile and Mint

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, more as needed
very large ripe tomato, cored and diced (1½ cups)

steps: Heat oven to 400 degrees. On rimmed baking sheet, toss together eggplant, 3 tablespoons olive oil, ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper. Spread into one layer. Roast, tossing occasionally, until the eggplant is golden brown, about 25 minutes.
Place tomato in large bowl and sprinkle lightly with salt.
Bring large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne to al dente according to package instructions; drain well.

While pasta cooks, heat large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons oil. Stir in garlic, anchovies and chile flakes, and cook until golden and soft, about 3 minutes. Turn off heat and, using slotted spoon, transfer garlic to cutting board. Let garlic cool for a few minutes, then chop up and add back to the oil. Pour garlic-chile into bowl with tomatoes. Add eggplant and capers, and toss well.
Add pasta to bowl with eggplant and tomatoes. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice to taste, and drizzle generously with oil. Toss in herbs and serve warm or at room temperature.

miso-glazed-salmon-with-jasmine-rice-and.title: Miso-Glazed Salmon With Jasmine Rice and Sesame Spinach
miso-glazed-salmon-with-jasmine-rice-and.description: A complete weeknight dinner: broiled miso salmon over fluffy jasmine rice, with garlicky sesame spinach, timed so everything finishes together.
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with the water and salt in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce to the lowest heat, and cook without lifting the lid, 15 minutes.

While the rice cooks, whisk the miso, mirin, honey, 1 teaspoon of the soy sauce, rice vinegar and ginger. Pat the salmon dry and spread most of the glaze over the tops and sides, saving about a tablespoon. Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it, and line a sheet pan with foil brushed with 1 teaspoon of the oil.
When the rice is done, take the pan off the heat and let it sit, still covered, for 10 minutes while you cook the salmon and spinach.

Broil the salmon skin-side down until the glaze is browned in spots and the fish just flakes at the thickest part (about 125°F for medium), about 7 minutes. Tent with foil if the glaze darkens too fast.

While the salmon broils, heat the remaining 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant and just golden. Add the spinach a few handfuls at a time, tossing until just wilted, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and season with the sesame oil and the remaining 1 teaspoon soy sauce.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Divide rice and spinach between plates, set the salmon on top, and brush with the reserved glaze. Finish with the scallions and sesame seeds.
tips: Thick center-cut fillets may need 8 to 10 minutes under the broiler; thin tail pieces 5 to 6.
A rice cooker works too, using its jasmine setting.
Spoon any glaze drippings from the foil over the rice.

To roast instead of broil: bake at 425°F for 10 to 14 minutes, until the salmon just flakes (about 125°F). The glaze is less likely to burn; for more caramelization, switch to broil for the last 1 to 2 minutes and watch closely. Line the pan with foil or parchment either way.
notes: Miso brands vary in saltiness, so taste the glaze first and add a little more honey if it's sharp.
Baby spinach shrinks a lot; use 1 pound for bigger portions.

meatballs-and-red-sauce.title: Sunday Sauce
meatballs-and-red-sauce.description: Beef and sausage meatballs simmered in a slow-baked tomato sauce enriched with pepperoni and bone-in pork chops.

ingredients.item: sweet Italian pork sausage, casings removed
large pasta, such as rigatoni or paccheri

steps: Preheat the oven to 275°F. In a large Dutch oven, heat the oil over medium-low heat. Brown the pork chops on both sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté the onions until translucent. Add the garlic and cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Remove half of the onion and garlic mixture and set it aside for the meatballs.

Add the tomato paste and stir until combined and aromatic, about 1 minute. Stir in the wine, scraping up any bits stuck to the bottom of the pot, and reduce by about half, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes and any juices, stir to combine, and bring the sauce to a boil.

Once the sauce is bubbling, add the pepperoni and place the pot in the oven for at least 4 hours, until the pepperoni is soft and flexible. Add the pork chops about 1½ hours before taking the sauce out of the oven.

To prepare the meatballs, heat the oven to 475°F (if needed, take the sauce out of the oven and keep it at a low simmer on the stove). Place the bread slices and milk in a large mixing bowl. Once the bread has absorbed the liquid, mash it with a fork.

Add the reserved onions and garlic, eggs, parsley, beef, sausage meat, grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Gently combine with your hands. Carefully form into 2-inch meatballs and place them on a baking sheet.
Bake the meatballs for 20 minutes. Transfer them directly into the sauce and simmer for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors combine. Meanwhile, boil water and cook the pasta.
Before serving, remove the pepperoni and pork chops from the sauce and slice them. Serve with the pasta, baguette and additional grated Parmesan.
notes: The sauce needs at least 4 hours in the oven, so start early.

alcatra-portuguese-style-beef-stew.title: Alcatra (Portuguese-Style Beef Stew)
alcatra-portuguese-style-beef-stew.description: Beef shank braised in white wine over onions with allspice, bay and cinnamon, finished with Spanish-style chorizo.

ingredients.item: Spanish-style chorizo sausage, cut into ¼-inch-thick rounds

steps: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 325 degrees. Trim away any fat or large pieces of connective tissue from exterior of shanks (silverskin can be left on meat). Cut each shank crosswise into 2½-inch pieces. Sprinkle meat with 1 teaspoon salt.

Cut an 8-inch square of triple-thickness cheesecloth. Place garlic, allspice berries, bay leaves, and peppercorns in center of cheesecloth and tie into bundle with kitchen twine. Arrange onions and spice bundle in Dutch oven in even layer. Add wine and cinnamon. Arrange shank pieces in single layer on top of onions. Cover and cook until beef is tender, about 3½ hours.

Remove pot from oven and add chorizo. Using tongs, flip each piece of beef over, making sure that chorizo is submerged. Cover and let stand until chorizo is warmed through, about 20 minutes. Discard spice bundle. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve.
tips: Substitution: 4 pounds of bone-in crosscut shank works if that’s all you can find. Remove the bones before cooking (save them for another use) and check for doneness after 3 hours, since crosscut shank cooks more quickly.
Substitution: a 3½- to 4-pound chuck roast, trimmed of fat and cut into 2½-inch pieces, can replace the shank.
Serving suggestion: crusty bread or boiled potatoes.
notes: Long-cut shank is preferred because it has more collagen.

mammas-ravioli.title: Mamma’s Ravioli
mammas-ravioli.description: Homemade cheese ravioli with a ricotta, mozzarella and parsley filling, boiled and finished in a casserole with tomato sauce. Makes 10 to 12 ravioli.
steps: Make the dough: Mix the flour, boiling water and salt. Knead well on a floured board, until a finger-puncture emerges clean. Let rest while mixing the filling.
Make the filling: In the same bowl, mix the ricotta, mozzarella, parsley, salt and pepper, eggs, and grated Romano or Parmesan well.
Cut off a chunk of dough and roll. If moist, sprinkle flour and roll more. Roll thin.
Place 3 dollops of cheese on the edge (1 tbsp each). Fold dough over the dollops and cut with a glass approximately 3 inches in diameter. Close with a fork.
Boil water with salt and 1 to 2 tbsp oil. When the water is fervently boiling, drop the raviolis in. Cover the pot.
When the raviolis rise to the top, continue cooking for 10 minutes. Remove with a ladle spoon and let drip.
Place in a casserole with tomato sauce.
notes: Eggs: you may need only one. Test: if you can take a clean spoonful of cheese, do not add the second egg. If too thick, add the second egg.

sausage-with-warm-beet-salad-and-garlick.title: Sausage With Warm Beet Salad and Garlicky Beet Greens
sausage-with-warm-beet-salad-and-garlick.description: A fall oven dinner that uses the whole bunch of beets: the roots roasted whole, peeled and dressed warm with goat cheese and walnuts, the greens sautéed with garlic and chile, and Italian sausage roasted alongside.

ingredients.item: beets with greens attached (about 6 medium beets)
sweet or hot Italian sausage links
sherry or red wine vinegar, divided
kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste

steps: Heat oven to 400 degrees. Cut the greens from the beets, leaving about an inch of stem, and scrub the beets (don’t peel). Wrap the beets in a foil packet with a splash of water, set on a rimmed sheet pan, and roast until a knife slides easily into the largest beet, about 55 minutes.

While the beets roast, wash the greens well, chop the stems into ½-inch pieces, and roughly chop the leaves, keeping stems and leaves separate. In a large bowl, whisk the shallot, 1½ tablespoons vinegar, the mustard, honey and a pinch of salt. Let the shallot soften in the vinegar, then whisk in 1½ tablespoons olive oil.

When the beets are nearly done, prick the sausages a few times with a fork and lay them on a foil-lined sheet pan. Roast alongside the beets, turning once halfway, until browned and cooked through (160 degrees), about 25 minutes.

Pull the beets and sausage from the oven and tent the sausage with foil. Open the beet packet and let the beets cool until you can handle them, about 10 minutes, then rub the skins off with a paper towel. Cut into ¾-inch wedges and toss while still warm with the dressing, ½ teaspoon salt and the pepper.

While the beets cool, heat the remaining 1½ tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium (add a spoonful of the sausage pan drippings for extra flavor). Add the beet stems and cook until starting to soften, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and red-pepper flakes and cook 30 seconds, then add the leaves in handfuls with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt, tossing until wilted. Finish with the remaining ½ tablespoon vinegar.
Scatter the walnuts and goat cheese over the warm beets. Slice the sausage and serve with the beet salad and greens.
tips: Serve with: [[roasted-sweet-potatoes-with-smoked-paprika]]. That recipe calls for 425 degrees; at 400 degrees alongside the beets, give the potatoes 5 to 10 minutes longer.
Beet size: small beets may be done in 40 minutes, large ones can take over an hour. Check with a knife rather than the clock.
Peeling: wear gloves or use a paper towel to avoid stained hands. Golden beets work too and bleed less.

shepherds-pie.title: Shepherd’s Pie
shepherds-pie.description: Ground lamb simmered in a rich gravy with carrots, peas and thyme, topped with buttery mashed potatoes and baked until golden.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks
unsalted butter, plus 2 tablespoons for dotting
kosher salt, plus more for the potato water
kosher salt, plus more to taste

steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by an inch, and salt the water generously. Bring to a boil, then simmer until a knife slides in easily, about 18 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat oven to 400 degrees. Heat the olive oil in a large (12-inch) ovenproof skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high. Add the lamb, breaking it up, and cook until well browned, about 8 minutes. Spoon off all but about 2 tablespoons of the fat.
Add the onion and carrots and cook, stirring, until softened, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook, stirring, until the paste darkens, about 1 minute.

Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, rosemary, 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until thick and glossy, about 10 minutes. Stir in the peas and taste for salt.
Drain the potatoes well and return to the pot for a minute to steam dry. Mash with 4 tablespoons butter, the milk and 1 teaspoon salt until smooth, then beat in the egg yolk.

If you used a Dutch oven, transfer the filling to a 9-by-13-inch baking dish; otherwise leave it in the skillet. Spoon the potatoes over the filling, starting at the edges to seal it in, then spread evenly. Rough up the top with a fork and dot with the remaining 2 tablespoons butter.
Set on a foil-lined sheet pan and bake until the filling bubbles at the edges and the top is golden, about 25 minutes. For more color, broil for the last 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely.
Let rest about 10 minutes before serving so the filling sets.
tips: Cottage pie: use ground beef instead of lamb; everything else stays the same.
Egg yolk: it helps the potato top brown and hold its shape, but you can skip it.
Make ahead: assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate, then add 10 to 15 minutes to the baking time.

pork-milanese-with-arugula-salad.title: Pork Milanese With Arugula Salad
pork-milanese-with-arugula-salad.description: Bone-in pork chops pounded thin, breaded in panko and Parmesan and fried until crisp, topped with a lemony arugula, tomato and Parmesan salad.

ingredients.item: bone-in pork rib or center-cut chops, about ¾ inch thick (8 to 10 ounces each)
kosher salt, plus more for finishing
finely grated Parmesan, plus shavings for serving
neutral oil or olive oil, for frying
small red onion, very thinly sliced
lemon, half juiced, half cut into wedges

steps: Heat oven to 400 degrees and set a wire rack on a sheet pan. Trim any thick fat cap from the chops and make a few small cuts through the fat at the edge so they don’t curl. Place each chop between sheets of plastic wrap and pound the meat (not the bone) with a meat mallet to an even ½-inch thickness, leaving the bone attached. Season both sides with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
Put the flour in a shallow dish. In a second dish, beat the eggs with the water. In a third, mix the panko and grated Parmesan, crushing the panko a little with your hand.

Dredge each chop in flour and shake off the excess, dip in egg and let the excess drip off, then press firmly into the crumbs to coat both sides, working around the bone. Let sit 5 minutes so the coating sets.

Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high until the butter foams. Fry 2 chops at a time until deep golden and crisp, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer to the rack and repeat with the rest, adding a little more oil if the pan gets dry.
Put the chops on the rack into the oven until the meat near the bone reaches 140 degrees, 5 to 8 minutes. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and let rest 5 minutes (they’ll climb to 145 degrees).
While the chops rest, toss the arugula, tomatoes and red onion with the juice from half the lemon, the olive oil and ½ teaspoon salt.
Put a chop on each plate, pile the arugula salad on top, and finish with Parmesan shavings. Serve with lemon wedges.
tips: Pork tenderloin instead: use 1¼ pounds, cut crosswise into 4 pieces and pounded to ¼ inch. Fry about 3 minutes per side; at that thickness it cooks through in the pan, so skip the oven.
Chicken Milanese: chicken breasts work the same way.

classic-deviled-eggs.title: Classic Deviled Eggs
classic-deviled-eggs.description: Creamy, tangy yolk filling piped into tender egg whites and finished with paprika and chives. Makes 12 halves.

ingredients.item: white wine vinegar or pickle juice
unsalted butter, softened (optional, for extra-silky filling)
kosher salt, plus more to taste
paprika or smoked paprika, for garnish

steps: Bring a medium pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower the eggs in with a spoon, reduce to a steady simmer, and cook 12 minutes.
Transfer the eggs to a bowl of ice water and let them chill completely, about 10 minutes; this makes them easier to peel and keeps the yolks bright yellow.
Crack the eggs all over and peel under cool running water. Pat dry, slice in half lengthwise, and pop the yolks into a bowl. Arrange the whites on a platter.

Mash the yolks with a fork until very fine (or press through a sieve for the smoothest texture). Stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, butter if using, salt, pepper and hot sauce until creamy. Taste and adjust salt and vinegar.

Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites (a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off works fine). Dust with paprika and scatter the chives over the top. Serve right away or refrigerate, covered, up to 4 hours.
tips: Easy peeling: starting the eggs in boiling water instead of cold makes them much easier to peel.
Variations: fold in crumbled bacon, top with a sliver of cornichon, or swap Greek yogurt for half the mayo.
Make ahead: keep the filling and whites separate, covered, for up to a day, and fill before serving.

slow-cooker-chili.title: Slow-Cooker Chili
slow-cooker-chili.description: Ground beef and beans simmered low and slow with beer, a deep mix of spices, a little cocoa and maple, finished with Worcestershire and all the toppings.

ingredients.item: large yellow or red onion, finely chopped
ground beef, 80 percent lean, 20 percent fat
(1½ cups) pilsner beer, such as Modelo Especial
(14-ounce) diced or crushed tomatoes in juice
maple syrup or dark brown sugar
beef stock bouillon paste, such as Better Than Bouillon
Hot sauce, grated sharp Cheddar, sliced scallions, sour cream and crushed tortilla chips, for serving

steps: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium. Add the onion, season with salt, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and translucent, about 8 minutes. Increase the heat to medium-high, add the beef and garlic, season with salt and cook, breaking the beef into crumbles with a spatula, until the beef has lost its pink color, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until slightly darkened and caramelized, about 1 minute. Stir in all the spices and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the beer and stir, scraping the bottom of the pan.

Transfer the beef mixture into a 5- to 8-quart slow-cooker. Stir in the tomatoes, vinegar, maple syrup, soy sauce, beef bouillon paste, cocoa, beans and ½ cup water. Cover and cook on low for at least 4 hours and up to 6 hours. (The chili can hold well on warm for an additional 2 hours.)

When ready to serve, stir in the Worcestershire sauce. If the chili is too thick, stir in a bit of water until the texture is to your liking. Season to taste with salt. Serve in bowls and pass the toppings at the table.
tips: Stovetop: You can also cook the chili in a Dutch oven on your stovetop in about 1 hour. In step 2, add 1 cup water instead of 1/2 cup and let the mixture come to a simmer over medium-high. (Because the cooking liquid reduces further on the stovetop, this method starts with more water.) Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook until the meat is tender, stirring occasionally, about 35 minutes.

spanish-chicken-chorizo-and-potato-stew.title: Spanish Chicken, Chorizo and Potato Stew
spanish-chicken-chorizo-and-potato-stew.description: Boneless chicken thighs braised with smoky Spanish chorizo, potatoes, peppers, white wine and smoked paprika until everything is tender and the broth is brick red.

ingredients.item: kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
Spanish-style (cured) chorizo, sliced into ¼-inch rounds
red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
pitted green olives, such as Manzanilla (optional)

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season all over with 1½ teaspoons salt and the pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium. Add the chorizo and cook, stirring, until it releases its red oil and starts to crisp, about 4 minutes. Move to a plate with a slotted spoon, leaving the oil in the pot.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and raise the heat to medium-high. Working in 2 batches so the pot isn’t crowded, brown the chicken without moving it until deep golden on the first side, about 4 minutes, then flip and cook 2 minutes more. It doesn’t need to cook through. Move to the plate with the chorizo.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and bell peppers with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until softened, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic, smoked paprika and tomato paste and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom of the pot; simmer 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, broth, potatoes, bay leaves and saffron if using (crumble it in). Return the chicken, chorizo and any juices from the plate and stir to submerge.
Bring to a simmer, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is very tender, about 25 minutes.

Uncover, stir in the olives if using, and simmer 5 minutes to thicken slightly. Discard the bay leaves and taste for salt. Scatter with the parsley and serve in shallow bowls with lemon wedges and crusty bread.
tips: Chorizo: use cured Spanish chorizo (the firm, salami-like kind), not fresh Mexican chorizo, which crumbles and cooks differently.
Bone-in thighs: use 2½ pounds bone-in, skin-on thighs. Brown skin side down about 8 minutes, nestle them in skin side up above the liquid, and braise about 35 minutes.
Make ahead: it’s even better the next day.
notes: Thighs stay juicy through the braise, so don’t swap in breasts, which dry out.
